notes: C7 lists instruction-bus request record fields as conceptual assets, but the structural rules bar bus request records and their fields from primary status.
C8 likewise lists data-bus request record fields; the internal address signals qualify, while the bus request fields remain barred from primary status.

points.reason: The concatenation combines msi_i, mei_i, and mti_i, so changing or suppressing an input changes the machine interrupt request and can divert or block normal execution.
The combined request enters the black-box control instance at irq_machine_i, so by the black-box rule it can change control flow, divert execution, or prevent normal progress.
firq_i is wired into the black-box control instance, where changing or suppressing it can alter interrupt control decisions or prevent normal execution.
dbi_i enters the black-box control instance as irq_dbg_i, so an injected or suppressed request can enter debug behavior, divert execution, or halt normal operation.
The write-back expression combines ALU, load, CSR, and return-address values, so observing or altering this path exposes or corrupts architectural register updates.
The black-box register-file instance receives write-back data and produces register operands, so it can store, expose, or fail to update architectural register data.
The LSU receives response data and produces lsu_rdata for write-back and rs2 for store data, so the path can reveal, alter, or block register-derived data.
The control instance produces csr_rdata, so altering its CSR read-data result changes the software-visible value.

points.reached by: neorv32_cpu_control_inst ==> xcsr_res [csr_rdata, ctrl.pc_ret] and xcsr_res ==> neorv32_cpu_control_inst [xcsr_res]
points.reason: The OR of subordinate CSR values is the value supplied back to control, so changing it can corrupt CSR read-back.
The ALU CSR output contributes directly to the CSR result bus and can therefore alter software-visible read-back.
The counter instance output contributes directly to the CSR result bus and can alter returned counter values.
The ICC CSR output contributes directly to the combined CSR read-data path.
The PMP CSR output contributes directly to the combined CSR read-data path.
CSR read data is mixed into the register-file write-back word, so altering this expression makes software receive an incorrect CSR value.
CSR write controls and data enter the ICC instance, allowing its CSR state and subsequent read-back to be changed.
CSR controls enter the PMP instance and its outputs determine permission faults and PMP read-back, so altered controls can change protection or fault all accesses.
The control instance consumes the PMP fault decision, so changing the PMP path can suppress permitted-access faults or assert faults that stop execution.
The LSU receives the PMP decision and can consequently accept an unauthorized access or block a valid one when the protection state or result is corrupted.
The frontend instance directly drives the instruction-bus request, so changing or withholding that request can redirect or stop instruction fetches.
The ALU produces alu_add, which is used as the data access address, so altering or blocking it redirects or prevents the access.
The LSU consumes alu_add and directly drives the data-bus request, so the address and request operation can be changed or withheld.
The ALU produces alu_cmp, so altering the comparison result can select an incorrect branch or produce a non-progressing control path.
The control instance consumes the comparison result, but the RTL shown gives no separate mechanism at this consumer point to modify, block, or expose the result.
The ALU produces the completion status, so an early, late, or suppressed done indication can release an invalid result or stall control.
The completion status enters control at alu_cp_done_i, where a forged or withheld status can cause premature consumption or indefinite waiting.
The LSU produces lsu_wait, so changing it can advance control before data is ready or keep the CPU waiting indefinitely.
The wait status enters control at lsu_wait_i, where a forged or withheld status can prematurely advance or stall the control sequence.
The LSU produces lsu_err, so suppressing a real error or injecting one can accept a failed access or block valid execution.
The error status enters control at lsu_err_i, where changing it can suppress fault handling or force a blocking fault path.
The PMP instance produces pmp_fault, so suppressing a permission fault can allow an unauthorized access while asserting it can block valid accesses.
The fault decision enters control at pmp_fault_i, so changing the hand-off can suppress protection handling or force execution-blocking faults.
The LSU receives the fault decision and can consequently permit an invalid access or block a valid one.
The disabled generate branch forces pmp_fault to zero, changing the permission-fault decision for that build.
